text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - UK blue chips finished at a record high for the third straight session on Wednesday as the market continued to celebrate the British government's decision to take interest rate policy out of the political arena. A weak start on Wall Street dragged UK shares off their day's best levels but the FTSE 100 still managed to end 18.2 points firmer to a record closing level of 4,537.5.

FRANKFURT - German shares took a break from their recent turbulence on Wednesday as activity slowed ahead of Thursday's national holiday. The blue chip DAX index eased to close the bourse session down 16.30 points at 3,551.98 points, with business firmly focused on companies at the centre of the day's news. In post-bourse trade the index fell 11.07 to 3,537.45.

PARIS - French shares closed 0.33 percent lower on Wednesday in a directionless market which was affected just before the close by a lower opening on Wall Street and an easier dollar, dealers said. Brokers noted many investors squaring their positions as they prepared a long weekend break on the back of the Ascension day holiday on Thursday, amid some uncertainty about pending opinion polls for the May 25/June 1 parliamentary election. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 8.62 points at 2,643.31.

ZURICH - Swiss shares shrugged off Tuesday's weakness to close a shortened session firmer with the blue chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) climbing above the psychologically important level of 5,000 points. "There seems to be just one direction," a dealer said about the market's renewed rise. "But this may also be a bit dangerous," he warned.

The Swiss bourse had posted four straight record-breaking sessions before Tuesday's correction. "Everything that comes down is being bought," another trader said. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 16.51 points to 3,167.28.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended down on Wednesday after the key index had racked up huge gains in the past five sessions, brokers said. They said profit-taking emerged in some blue-chip issues to send the Nikkei average briefly below the 20,000 threshold in the afternoon. The 225-share Nikkei average fell 132.02 points to 20,048.90.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed modestly higher on Wednesday after trading sideways throughout most of the day as the market took a breather following hefty gains over the previous five sessions, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index rose 26.57 points, to close at 13,605.91 after see-sawing between 13,533 and 13,649.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market ended at its second successive record closing high on Wednesday. Bank shares continued their recent strong run as investors tipped higher dividends ahead of the latest round of results. The All Ordinaries index ended 4.8 points up at 2,517.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended soft in what dealers said was a disappointing market. Industrials eased, continuing the sell-off seen before the close on Tuesday on a weaker Wall Street opening. Golds were softer depressed by a dull bullion price hovering around the $340 an ounce level.

Dealers said volumes were high boosted by asset swaps, corporate finance deals and some futures play. Direction of market difficult to call for Thursday after Wednesday's sell-off. All-shares closed down 51.2 points to 7,160.7, industrials lost 65.1 points to 8,503.6 and golds dropped 23.0 points to 1,189.3.
